s: Physics' best theory of particles, the Standard Model, works very well. But it has about two dozen numbers we have to
because nothing explains them. The most famous is the
, which sets how strongly light and electric charge interact. Richard Feynman called it "a magic number that comes to us with no understanding by man."
AWG proposes that, at bottom, the universe is
nothing but a finite number of tiny quantum objects linked in pairs by perfect entanglement
, like the links of chainmail. Particles aren't vibrating
(as in string theory); they're small patterns of
. And the only way anything is ever "known" is by linking to it. There's no observer standing outside the network.
"Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them."
That sentence is the whole input. "Qudit" means a quantum bit that can have 2, 3, 4… states instead of just 2.

Take the one special link where a 3-state qudit is entangled with a 2-state qudit. Count, in a precise way, every possible "measurement record" two reads can leave on it. The count produces this number:
Measured (CODATA 2022): 1 / 137.035 999 177(21). They agree to about 10 significant digits.
the fine-structure constant. The arithmetic is machine-checked (in the Lean proof language). The claim that it's the
α is a conjecture, to be tested by future measurements.
Past attempts to "derive" 1/137 failed because they had something to tune. This one claims nothing is tuned.
The formula fixes every digit in advance. New experiments aim to be up to ten times more precise. If they drift away from 137.035 999 189…, the conjecture is dead.

The same link has exactly the symmetry group of the Standard Model, SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1). The 754-page compendium sketches how quantum mechanics, spacetime, gravity, three generations of matter, and more might also come out.
It's brand new (Oct 23, 2026) and hasn't been vetted by other physicists yet.
"Numerology" has a long history: people have found many formulas close to 1/137. AWG argues his is different because it follows from stated rules, but whether those rules are the
Of the compendium's 407 graded results, 100 are called theorems, 109 are conditional on stated assumptions, and 198 are open. Many links to real particles are "by name only."
is a physicist and computer scientist (PhD in physics from Harvard) and a regular voice on Peter Diamandis's
. In October 2026 he released three documents:
: "A Parameter-Free Candidate for the Fine-Structure Constant from Entangled Qudits" (24 pages including the Supplemental Material), dated Oct 23, 2026. This is the sharp, short claim.

: "Chain Theory: Toward Fundamental Physics from Distilling Networks of Entangled Qudits. A Compendium of Preliminary Findings." Working draft, 754 pages, sixteen Parts plus appendices and 52 "instrument" chapters.

AWG frames the project historically. From 1900 to 1928, physics was rebuilt from the ground up: Planck's quantum (1900), special relativity (1905), Bohr's atom (1913), general relativity (1915), quantum mechanics (1925), and Dirac's equation (1928). Over the next decades those became the Standard Model, whose structure was essentially complete by the mid-1970s.

Since then, he argues, physics has had confirmation but no new structure. The W and Z bosons (1983), top quark (1995), Higgs boson (2012) and gravitational waves (2015) were all predicted decades earlier. The genuine surprises, neutrino masses and the accelerating expansion (both 1998), were explained by no theory and
Faced with that, the field largely shifted from

them: anthropic arguments, the string-theory landscape of many possible vacua, and the "swampland" program. AWG's stance is the opposite. Keep derivation as the goal, and look for new foundations instead.
3. Three clues hiding in plain sight
AWG argues that existing physics already contains three hints, each of which has been read as something else.

Bekenstein (1981) showed a bounded region can hold only finitely much information. Holography ('t Hooft, Susskind), gravity from thermodynamics (Jacobson 1995), and "spacetime from entanglement" (Van Raamsdonk 2010) all build on this. Fields have infinitely many degrees of freedom and strings infinitely many modes.
Clue 2 · A gauge group: the Standard Model's "ugly" symmetry

The Standard Model's symmetry group is SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) (more precisely, divided by ℤ₆). Grand Unified Theories treated this lumpy product as a blemish to hide inside one bigger group (SU(5), SO(10)…). Those theories predicted proton decay and superpartners, and neither has been seen.
the set of independent "basis changes" you can make at the two ends of
one qutrit (3 states) perfectly entangled with one qubit (2 states)
. That gives SU(3) at one end, SU(2) at the other, and one leftover phase that belongs to the pair rather than either end. So the gauge group is a signature of a single entangled pair.
Clue 3 · A null result: particles show no parts

Every elementary particle looks like a point, even at the highest collider energies. Yet three generations repeating the same pattern of charges is exactly the sort of thing that usually means constituents (think periodic table → protons/neutrons → quarks).
Quantum information has a kind of correlation,

(Horodecki, Horodecki & Horodecki, 1998), that is genuinely entangled yet can't be "distilled" into a usable entangled pair by any local operations. It first becomes possible when the two systems' dimensions multiply to more than 6. AWG's reading: the substructure of matter isn't
. Scattering would see a point, while a suitable "entanglement witness" could in principle show the structure.
Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them.
The building blocks are quantum systems with a finite number of states: qubits (2), qutrits (3), ququarts (4), and so on.
They only come in perfectly entangled pairs, called
. Partial entanglement would introduce continuous numbers, which a fully discrete theory can't afford.
A qudit can be the end of several links, so pairs join into networks ("webs"). This is the chainmail.
The only thing that ever happens is "distillation": projecting two qudits into a perfectly entangled pair in one step. It's the same move as
in quantum networks. In a lab it succeeds only sometimes (probability 1/d²); in the theory it's the only thing that ever happens. Consequence: there is no external observer.
To know something is to link to it.
The model also says time isn't assumed. Acts on separate qudits can be reordered freely, like rewriting 2·3·3·2 = 36 in different groupings. The compendium tries to
time as steps between acts (graded conditional).
Distillation as entanglement swapping: projecting qudits 2 and 3 into an entangled pair leaves 1 and 4 entangled, although they never touched.
The name has three sources (from the talk and preface):
Particles are finite chainmail made of discrete links, not continuous strings.
Where pairs meet at a shared qudit, nothing fixes how the bases line up, just as two chain links can turn against each other without changing the chain. That freedom is the theory's
A distillation passes its basis outward along each link, so knowledge accumulates in a fixed order, "the way a chained ledger grows by linking each new entry to the last."
6. Six kinds of link, two you can see
is the pair of its end dimensions. Conjecture 0 of the compendium restricts ends to dimension 2, 3 or 4, which gives six genres. Each is
to correspond to a sector of physics:

the axiom says two ends are "known" only if every consistent relation between them is one a distillation can carry. Classic math theorems (Størmer 1963, Woronowicz 1976, Choi 1975) show this holds exactly when d₁·d₂ ≤ 6. That's the same threshold where bound entanglement becomes possible. So only spacetime (2,2) and electromagnetism (3,2) can be observed directly. The other four are "dark" and are seen only at second order, through two distillations. At (3,3) the theory reads this as
: you never see a lone quark.

Note the elegant coincidence AWG leans on: the boundary between "readable" and "dark" (product ≤ 6) is a theorem of pure mathematics. It happens to split off exactly the two forces we observe directly at long range, light and gravity.
Why pick α as the test? (From the talk.)
It's known to about one part in ten billion, yet the Standard Model simply takes it from experiment.
A simple value like Koide's 2/3 can come from many short formulas. Ten digits of 137.035 999… can't.
Older closed forms (Wyler 1969/71, and others) foundered because some volume or normalization could be rescaled. A real derivation has to leave nothing to fix.

The result. Among all configurations of readable links, exactly one satisfies three conditions: it is a two-point function, it is read at the qutrit end, and every link carries an acting electric-type charge. That configuration is one shared qutrit with three links to qubits, two of them "read." Counting the measurement records two reads can leave gives 172 records, sorted by two symmetries into four groups of sizes 79, 48, 42 and 3, weighted 1, √2, √3 and √6. The total number of possible "directions" is 24·36·36 = 31104. So:
The comparison: CODATA 2022 recommends 1/α = 137.035 999 177 with uncertainty 21 in the last two digits. The candidate sits

away, between the two most precise measurements. But those measurements disagree with each other: cesium recoil (2018) and rubidium recoil (2020) are in tension. So the comparison isn't decisive yet. Upcoming measurements (electron g−2 at Northwestern; atomic recoil in Berkeley and Paris) aim to be up to 10× more precise.

The compendium's abstract lists results at three grades:

the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1); conservation laws; the second law of thermodynamics; band structure and the Chern number; phase transitions; a distillation theorem for quantum computation; "three generations as a theorem of the valence" (box 83.1).

the state space, Born rule, unitarity and uncertainty relation of quantum mechanics; the rotation and Lorentz groups; the signature of spacetime; parity, time reversal and CPT; the α candidate itself (as a physical identification); the electron's anomalous magnetic moment through third order; the hydrogen spectrum; parity violation; confinement; running of couplings; decay rates as finite sums with no renormalization; curvature; the cosmological term.
three generations, particle masses, and the "anatomies" (webs) of Standard Model particles.

Particles get proposed webs. For example, the electron is a core triangle of three qutrits (3,3), an in-leg (4,3) joining a "hub" to the core, hub legs (4,2), a qubit pair (2,2), and docks (3,2). The muon carries two hub assemblies and the tau three ("the lepton ladder"). The W and Z are one web read two different ways. A hadron is a "star": a junction qutrit carrying three quark bodies. All of these identifications are
. Of 17 particles drawn on 16 webs, 1 rests on a theorem, 11 on conditional theorems, 2 on open results and 3 on results not in this release.

Derived from the axiom and its definitions. 64 are tied to named Lean declarations.

the physical things (the α identification, the six sectors, the particle webs). Tested by measurement, not proved.

many theorems are exhaustive checks over the finite set of webs the compendium records. For example, the second law is checked at all 228 one-act reads of fourteen bodies. That's "a census of a finite catalog, not a proof for every web."
Also: "names from the literature are correspondences by name." When a box says "the Higgs" or "the weak interaction," it is a statement about networks that
after the physics. The physical identification is separate.

The Letter shows (in its "What else the count could have given" table) that small rewordings of the definitions give 1/α of 135.89, 139.03, 146.52, 97.51, 180.84 and so on. AWG argues each alternative is excluded by a definition
comparing with α. A skeptic will ask whether the definitions were chosen knowing the target. Two of the alternatives land within 1%.
The talk says so directly: the Lean file checks that the definitions produce the number, not that they're the right physics. The photon conjecture "appears nowhere in it."
The link carries hypercharge, not electric charge.

The talk notes the object's charge is the hypercharge direction, and "its passage to electric charge, together with spacetime and helicity, lies beyond the Letter." That's a real gap between the math object and the photon.
α changes with energy. The Letter targets α(0), the zero-momentum (Thomson-limit) value, via the on-shell scheme. That choice is principled, but it's another place to check the reasoning.
Ten digits is a lot of evidence
the formula wasn't selected from many candidates. How you weigh it depends on how much freedom you think the construction had.

At release this was a self-published preprint and draft. Secondary coverage notes AWG co-founded Physical Superintelligence (psi.inc), and that the work was developed with AI assistance. Independent audits were being called for online.

Part 2 · The cross product, and why it's antisymmetric
Given two 3D vectors a and b, the cross product a × b is a third vector perpendicular to both. Its length is |a||b| sin θ, and its direction comes from the right-hand rule. In components:
a × b = (a_y b_z − a_z b_y, a_z b_x − a_x b_z, a_x b_y − a_y b_x)
Two things to notice. Each component is a
, such as a_x b_y − a_y b_x. And because of that:
A vector crossed with itself is zero:
a × a = 0, since each component becomes x − x.
Example: x̂ × ŷ = ẑ, ŷ × ẑ = x̂, ẑ × x̂ = ŷ, while ŷ × x̂ = −ẑ.
Take n directions e₁…eₙ and write every ordered pair eᵢeⱼ. There are n² of them. Swapping the two places sorts them into two kinds:

With three directions x, y, z, the 9 cells of the grid split into 6 symmetric and 3 antisymmetric:
The diagonal cells are symmetric on their own. The 6 off-diagonal cells pair up across the diagonal: each pair gives one symmetric combination (xy + yx) and one antisymmetric one (xy − yx).
The 3 antisymmetric combinations are yz − zy, zx − xz and xy − yx. Those are exactly the x, y and z components of a cross product. The cross product
the antisymmetric part of a pair of 3D vectors. As the talk puts it, Λ²3 = 3 is "the three components of a cross product."

4. What must be computed: the on-shell coupling
For a massless spin-1 field coupled to a conserved abelian charge, the zero-transfer coupling is universal (Weinberg 1964–65). The Ward identity Z₁ = Z₂ reduces it to vacuum polarization:

glossary.d: The dimensionless strength of electromagnetism, ≈ 1/137.036. α(0) is its value at zero momentum transfer (the Thomson limit), the one measured by low-energy experiments. α grows slowly at higher energies ("running").
The single input: "Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them."

Entanglement that's real (certifiable by a witness) but cannot be distilled into pure entangled pairs by local operations and classical communication, from any number of copies. Possible only when d₁d₂ > 6. AWG's model for why particle substructure is invisible.
In the "copy model," every link joins one ket end and one bra end, like indices of a tensor.
The international committee that recommends best values for fundamental constants every four years. CODATA 2022: 1/α = 137.035 999 177(21).
One of the 3 extra records at the qubits: two reads in different bases anticommute (XZ = −ZX), so their commutator is fixed too, with a sign set by the order of reads. Weight √6.
A result derived under conditions that are named in its box. A composite claim takes the lowest grade in its chain.
The fact that quarks are never seen alone. In Chain Theory, read as the (3,3) genre being "dark": no read survives at first order.
A link type whose ends are related by some non-decomposable positive map (d₁d₂ ≥ 8), so a single read can't fix them. Seen only at second order. (4,2), (3,3), (4,3), (4,4).

A positive map that's a sum of a completely positive map and a completely positive map composed with transpose. Every positive map is decomposable in dimensions 2×2 and 2×3 (Størmer, Woronowicz), but not beyond.

In the axiom: project two qudits onto the maximally entangled state on their common support, in one step, with no failure branch. Equivalent to the projection in entanglement swapping. In standard QI, "distillation" means extracting good pairs from many noisy copies; AWG generalizes it.
The bare insertion is the identity, weighing every one of N directions once. The dressed insertion M weighs only what the reads fix (the 172 records, weighted). Their ratio is the readout.
Measuring qudits 2 and 3 of pairs (1,2) and (3,4) in an entangled basis leaves 1 and 4 entangled. The basic move of quantum repeaters, and the act of the axiom.
The symmetry that swaps two links at the shared qutrit (moving their far-end qubits). Carries d = 2, giving weight √2 to symmetric records it acts on.
Swaps the order/identity of the two reads. Acts at the qutrit (where reads are taken), carries d = 3, giving weight √3.
The configuration of Theorem 1: a qutrit of degree three with three (3,2) arms, two read and one held (unread).
To determine with certainty from a single copy, not to estimate statistically over many.
The symmetry group of the Standard Model, (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1))/ℤ₆. In Chain Theory, the group of basis changes at the two ends of a qutrit–qubit pair, S(U(3)×U(2)).
The 8 traceless Hermitian 3×3 matrices that form a basis for su(3). The "letters" at a qutrit.
A link's type, the pair of its end dimensions written larger first: (2,2), (3,2), (4,2), (3,3), (4,3), (4,4).
A recurring sub-web in the conjectured particle webs. Each fermion generation adds one hub assembly (electron 1, muon 2, tau 3: "the lepton ladder").
The U(1) charge of the Standard Model before electroweak symmetry breaking. The central charge of the (3,2) link is 6iY.
What reads fix jointly, unchanged under every matching and every exchange of reads or pairs.
A proof assistant / programming language that machine-checks mathematical proofs. Used here to verify the finite computations (64 theorems tied to Lean declarations).
(1) A traceless operator basis element at a slot: Gell-Mann at a qutrit, Pauli at a qubit. (2) "The alpha Letter," the short paper with the α result.
Two qudits in the maximally entangled state |ω_m⟩ on their common support.
A change of basis U on a pair's support, acting as U⊗Ū. It leaves the pair unchanged, which is the gauge freedom at the joins.
|ω_m⟩ = (1/√m) Σ|i⟩|i⟩. Each end on its own is completely random, while together they're perfectly correlated.
A system maximally entangled with one partner can't be entangled with another. Why a shared qudit is carried as one copy per pair.
Bases in which measuring one tells you nothing about the other. A d-level system has up to d+1 of them; one read per MUB.
The convention defining α by the physical (zero-momentum) photon coupling: α(0) = Z₃·α_bare after the Ward identity.
A statement carried to a named step that remains open: neither established nor excluded.
X, Y, Z, the 3 traceless Hermitian 2×2 matrices. The "letters" at a qubit.
Projected entangled pair states: a tensor-network construction where each site holds several virtual qudits, each maximally entangled with a neighbor. The model of a shared qudit.
That the qutrit–qubit link of Theorem 1 is the elementary link of the photon, so its readout is α(0).
A linear map on operators that sends positive operators to positive operators. Every "consistent relation" between two ends is one.
Quantum systems with 2 / 3 / 4 / d states. AWG also calls them registers two, three, four.
An act at one end of a pair, distilling the two ends in a basis of that end, passing the basis along. Taken at the larger end.
The theorem that a genre is readable iff d₁d₂ ≤ 6: only (2,2) and (3,2).
⟨M⟩ = Tr_R M / dim R, the dressed-over-bare normalized trace.
Two letters at two different slots, the two insertions of a two-point function. 169 products + 3 commutators = 172.
The compendium's instrument mapping each Chain Theory noun to its nearest standard concept.
Compendium machinery. A seeded web is grown by moves ("waves") until it reaches a sink, a stable endpoint. Particles are proposed to be sinks; decay is a forward edge out of a non-sink.
One of the four ends where letters sit: Q₁, q₁, Q₂, q₂.
The established theory of quarks, leptons, and the electromagnetic, weak and strong forces plus the Higgs. About two dozen measured parameters.
Averaging over all matchings U⊗Ū. Since pairs are invariant, every readout is twirl-invariant, so reads see only 𝟙 and the pair projector.
A consequence of charge conservation (Z₁ = Z₂) that makes the charge's renormalization depend only on the photon's vacuum polarization Z₃.
A network of pairs joined at shared qudits. The nearest standard term is a graph state / tensor network. Particles are conjectured to be specific webs.
Standard deviations of measurement uncertainty. 0.6σ means the candidate is well within the error bar.

parts: Front matter
Preface, abstract, introduction, the Rosetta glossary, chapter maps and the register matrix. Start here: AWG's preface (pp. 2–5) is the clearest plain-language overview anywhere.
Part I. The Framework

Everything descends from the axiom (Definition 1.1) and five definitions. Part I builds the shared objects: the link and its six genres, the read cap, records and the 'gain lemma' (Born count), the moves between webs, saturation to sinks, the register at which a probe reads, the classical limit, decoupling. No particles or forces yet.
Part II. The Rule, the Chain Automata and the Single Root
Tables only in this release: lists four instrument chapters (chain automata, the move table, locality, light cone, regeneration) printed at the end.
Part III. Quantum Mechanics

Can textbook QM be read off the framework instead of postulated? State space as the span of act outputs (35.1), the Born rule and unitarity, uncertainty from the Weyl relation, measurement as 'the wash at one act' (theorem 28.1), indistinguishability and spin-statistics, energy, the path integral as a finite record sum, the Wigner function. Mostly conditional: 'the Born rule is an output, conditional on its premises, not an input.'
Part IV. Spacetime, Symmetry and the Dynamics of the Read

'Nothing in the axiom mentions space.' Time as an order coordinate counting steps (50.1), the rotation group, the Lorentz group as isometries of the Hermitian split (signature one-against-three at the qutrit–qubit link, 54.1/55.1), boosts, spin and helicity, the spin-c group, P, C, T and CPT.
Part V. The Matrix: the Standard Model at the Six Genres

Gauge theory read backwards from its premises. Gauge invariance as the 'known' clause (64.1), the gauge group as the face group of the qutrit–qubit tether, S(U(2)×U(3)) (64.2, theorem), representations as a census of open ends, Cartan weights and charge, conservation as the kernel of the move matrix (74.1), the Ward identity, anomaly cancellation, and 'Three, a theorem of the valence' (83.1): three generations from three core sites.
Part VI. The Metric, the Worldline and the Horizon: the (2,2) cell

Gravity 'as a statement about counting.' A metric from the depth of a web, curvature as a graph Laplacian (90.2), the field equation at the 'counting face', the area law, the horizon as a seeded saturation at every rung (99.1), abundances and rate at the horizon (104.1, theorem), the cosmological term at the depth exponent (115.1), dark sinks, the expansion rate. The correspondence to spacetime is conjectured.
Part VII. The Photon: the (3,2) cell

Where the construction 'first meets a number.' The coupling at the one link (the α result, including earlier editions of the Lean derivation), the electron's anomalous magnetic moment, the hydrogen ladder, Lamb shift and Casimir effect, finiteness of the sums, running of the coupling, the photon itself, the charged-lepton ladder as hub assemblies, and the Koide class.
Part VIII. The Carriers and the Breaking: the (4,2) cell

The weak interaction as the 'hub step', the move that attaches or detaches a junction and changes generation. Carriers (W/Z as one web read two ways), doublets, handedness and parity violation, the weak angle, mixing, beta decay, widths, the electroweak table. 'The most names attached by correspondence and the fewest theorems.'
Part IX. The Junction: the (3,3) cell

The strong force. The one genre where no read survives at first order, read as confinement (171.1). A hadron is a 'star': a junction qutrit of degree three carrying three quark bodies. Strong coupling, nucleon structure, the proton as a seeded sink (open), the proton/electron mass ratio candidate, the hadron spectrum, quark flavors.
Part X. The Yukawa Leg and the Higgs Offices at the Bodies: the (4,3) cell

'Mass is a read.' The mass unit and first power (185.1), the body-alone office rule (195.1, theorem), next-order terms, generation as depth momentum (197.1), and the unified mass readout (198.3). No measured mass is used as input.
Part XI. The Higgs, its Hub Register and the Dressing Field: the (4,4) cell
The Higgs as the closed hub read (200.1). The Higgs quartic as an exact element of ℚ(√2,√3) at all 10,123 Higgs-form sinks (202.1, theorem).
Part XII. Decays and Nuclear Physics

'A body that is not a sink moves on.' Stability as being a sink of the move graph, decay rates as washed squares of reads with no renormalization, lifetimes and branching, the deuteron and alpha particle as pairing records, nuclear rows, fission/fusion and stellar bounds.
Part XIII. Thermodynamics

The second law as a non-decreasing boundary count of records under acts (217.1, theorem, checked exhaustively), the thermal state as a twirl fixed point, ensembles, phase transitions as a change of sink class (221.1), the distillation theorem at forward saturation, entropy and the arrow of time.
Part XIV. Condensed Matter and Atoms

'A lattice is a periodic sink.' Rings of copies, bands as spectra of the step generator (225.1), chains of pairs, the Chern number as the winding of the wash holonomy, the periodic table as joined-electron sinks, atoms as hydrogen probe webs.
Part XV. Quantum Information

Back home: closure of a web as computation (230.1), the moves as a gate set, whether the Hadamard is inside it, the read as the maximal distillation (233.2), read cost, the adiabatic theorem, holonomy of basis transport (235.2). The most theorems after Part I.
Part XVI. The Scorecard, the Open Results and What Remains

The ledger: re-tallies (100 · 109 · 198), open results by form and Part, the status matrix of the six genres, 'what the construction has not reached', and the conclusion. Use it as an index to any claim's standing.
Appendices
Including the hub-forming move as symmetry breaking, saturation in one figure (seeds, waves, termination, sinks), the sector-to-ends map, and Standard Model tables.
Instruments
52 instrument chapters: the machinery and tables behind the Parts (chain automata, decoherence and open systems, causal structure and covariance, the Lagrangian table, per-genre censuses).

decks.name: Basics
decks.desc: The 60-second ideas: what, who, the number.
qs: What is Chain Theory's single input?
One axiom about maximally entangled pairs of qudits
The whole construction starts from one sentence: "Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them."
Which famous constant does the alpha Letter target?
α ≈ 1/137.036 sets the strength of electromagnetism. Feynman called it "a magic number that comes to us with no understanding by man."
In the name "Chain Theory," particles are pictured as…
Finite chainmail of discrete entangled links
"A chain, not a string." Particles are finite networks of discrete links.
A quantum system with a finite number d ≥ 2 of states
Qubit = 2 states, qutrit = 3, ququart = 4, and so on. All are qudits.
How closely does the candidate 1/α match CODATA 2022?
It matches exactly, with zero uncertainty
137.035 999 189 6… vs 137.035 999 177(21): ten significant digits, 0.60 standard deviations.
What checks the arithmetic of the count?
A single Lean 4 file with no imports builds all 172 records and evaluates the readout exactly.
Is "this number IS the physical α" proved?
No, it's the Photon Conjecture, tested by measurement
No, AWG says it's a coincidence
The number is a theorem of the definitions. Its identification with α(0) is explicitly a conjecture.
Future α measurements converging away from 137.035 999 189…
The exact form has no uncertainty of its own. More precise α(0) measurements will either close in on it or rule it out.

decks.name: Big Picture
decks.desc: Clues, genres, grades, and the skeptic's view.
qs: Which is NOT one of AWG's three clues?
Finite information in a bounded region (Bekenstein)
No observed substructure in elementary particles
The three clues are a bound, a gauge group, and a null result.
The gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) is read as the symmetry of…
A qutrit maximally entangled with a qubit
Basis changes at the ends give SU(3) and SU(2), plus a relative phase that neither end owns.
"Bound entanglement" first becomes possible when d₁·d₂ exceeds…
Above 6 (Horodecki 1998). The same threshold sets the read cap.
Only d₁d₂ ≤ 6 is readable: (2,2), conjectured spacetime, and (3,2), conjectured electromagnetism. The other four are dark.
Which sector is conjectured for the dark (3,3) genre?
No read survives at first order at (3,3), which Part IX reads as confinement.
In the axiom, "distilling" two qudits is essentially…
The projection used in entanglement swapping
Project onto the maximally entangled state in one step, with no failure branch. In a lab it's a Bell-measurement outcome with probability 1/d².
How many results does the compendium grade as full theorems?
100 theorems, 109 conditional theorems, 198 open results. 64 theorems are tied to Lean declarations.
AWG's own caution about many of his "theorems":
They are exhaustive checks over a finite catalog of webs
E.g., the second law is checked at all 228 one-act reads of fourteen bodies: "a census of a finite catalog, not a proof for every web."
Why is the gap from "hypercharge" to the photon important?
The link's charge is the hypercharge direction; reaching electric charge lies beyond the Letter
Hypercharge is the same as mass
The talk says so directly: the passage to electric charge, together with spacetime and helicity, lies beyond the Letter.

decks.name: The Math
qs: How many measurement records does the count use?
169 products of two letters at different slots, plus 3 commutator records at the qubits.
Where do the 3 commutator records come from?
Two reads at a qubit anticommute (XZ = −ZX)
By the definition of "known," the commutator of two anticommuting reads is itself fixed, with a sign set by the order of the reads.
24 = (3²−1)(2²−1) for the unread link; 36 = (3·2)² for each read link.
How many "letters" sit at a qutrit end?
d² − 1 traceless basis elements: 8 at a qutrit, 3 (Paulis) at a qubit.
A shared qutrit with three links to qubits, two of them read
The "fine-structure star": two read links (the insertions) plus one unread link (the state).
Why does a record surviving an exchange get weight √d?
Its letter runs over d strands at amplitude 1/√d each: d·(1/√d) = √d
The strand picture: each strand of a pair carries 1/√d.
Which group of records has weight √3?
48 symmetric, one slot at each end
42 symmetric, both slots at one kind of end
The exchange of reads X acts at the qutrit (d = 3): Sym²8 + Sym²3 = 36 + 6 = 42.
Using weights k instead of √k gives 1/α ≈ …
97.51. AWG rejects it because k is a four-letter, four-point quantity. Try it in the calculator.
Why is (3,2) the one readable genre with an acting central charge?
Q acts as i(d₂ − d₁): zero at (2,2), nonzero at (3,2)
The center Q = i·diag(d₂𝟙, −d₁𝟙) acts on the link as the scalar i(d₂ − d₁).
The candidate α lies in which number field?

qs: A column vector describing a quantum state
A ket is a column of complex amplitudes. Its conjugate row is the bra ⟨ψ|.
For |ψ⟩ = a|0⟩ + b|1⟩, the probability of measuring 0 is…
Ket-bra gives a matrix. P_m = |ω_m⟩⟨ω_m| is the projector that "distilling" applies.
A qutrit paired with a qubit lives in a space of dimension…
Dimensions multiply under ⊗: 3 × 2 = 6. That is the edge of the read cap, d₁d₂ ≤ 6.
It cannot be factored into (state of A)(state of B). It is |ω₂⟩, the qubit-pair link.
The cross product is antisymmetric: swapping the inputs flips the sign.
How many antisymmetric pairs do 3 directions give (Λ²3)?
n(n−1)/2 = 3. These are the x, y, z components of a cross product.
[X, Y] = XY − YX for Pauli matrices equals…
Pauli commutators mirror the cross product: x̂ × ŷ = ẑ. Chain Theory's 3 commutator records come from this.
